core_obligations: Reduce to the case where T is quasi-compact: let T_0 be the common image of the factorizations and let T' be a quasi-compact open containing it, note that every S_n -> T factors through T', and observe that T' = S implies T' = T = S (proof lines 8283-8288).

For quasi-compact T, use that T -> S is separated and quasi-finite and apply Zariski's Main Theorem to factor T -> W -> S with W -> S finite and T -> W an open immersion, writing W = Spec(B) and viewing the factorizations S_n -> T as morphisms into W to obtain A -> B -> lim A_n = A (proof lines 8291-8304).

Identify T x_{W,h} S as an open subscheme of S containing the image of S_n -> S for all n, and conclude by showing that any open U of S containing the image of some S_n -> S equals S, which follows because (A, Ker(A -> A_n)) is a henselian pair and hence every closed point of S lies in that image (proof lines 8305-8315).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to quasi-compact T through a quasi-compact open containing the common image (proof lines 8283-8288).
Apply Zariski's Main Theorem to convert the monomorphism into an open immersion into a finite S-scheme (proof lines 8291-8304).
Reduce the conclusion to a statement about opens containing the image of S_n and use the henselian pair (proof lines 8305-8315).
difficulty_reason: For A = lim A_n a limit of a system of rings with surjective transition maps and locally nilpotent kernels, the lemma states that a monomorphism T -> S = Spec(A) which is locally of finite type and through which every Spec(A_n) -> S factors must satisfy T = S (statement lines 8273-8280). The proof first reduces to a quasi-compact open T' of T containing the common image of the factorizations, so that T may be assumed quasi-compact, and then that T -> S is separated and quasi-finite (proof lines 8283-8294). Zariski's Main Theorem in the form of the quasi-finite separated factorization gives T -> W -> S with W -> S finite and T -> W an open immersion, and writing W = Spec(B) turns the unique factorizations S_n -> T into a diagram A -> B -> lim A_n = A (proof lines 8295-8304). The conclusion is then reduced to the statement that an open U of S containing the image of some S_n -> S must be all of S, which holds because the pair (A, Ker(A -> A_n)) is henselian, so every closed point of S lies in the image of S_n -> S (proof lines 8305-8315). The reduction to a henselian pair statement is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
